image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a brown butterfly resting on dry grass and straw. The butterfly has its wings spread open (dorsal view), revealing a uniform dark brown coloration with distinct rows of small, circular eyespots (ocelli) on both the forewings and hindwings. The body is slender, hairy, and brown, positioned centrally between the wings. The antennae are visible at the head, appearing clubbed. The background consists of out-of-focus dry vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The antennae are clearly visible extending from the head. They exhibit the characteristic thickening at the tips (clubs) typical of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Satyrid butterfly with moderately sized wingspan.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall morphology, wing shape, and size relative to the surrounding grass blades are consistent with a medium-sized satyrid butterfly like the ringlet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wings are a consistent dark brown. There are clear rows of ocelli: two prominent ones on each forewing and a series of smaller ones along the margin of the hindwings. This matches the diagnostic pattern for Aphantopus hyperantus.

The body appears slender and distinctly hairy/furry, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (three tagmata).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head, thorax, and abdomen are distinguishable as separate segments, consistent with insect anatomy.
